config.grain_rationale: Each row is one ASIC credit licence (CRED_LIC_NUM) held by a licensee. The business participant is the licensee named in CRED_LIC_NAME; the licence number itself is the record identifier, not a business identifier.

record_id.rationale: CRED_LIC_NUM is present on 100% of rows and has 464 distinct values over 464 discovery records - unique per record.

fields.rationale: ASIC register name of the licensee, presented as a registered-style name (mostly '... PTY LTD'/'... LIMITED'); some rows are individuals (e.g. 'TAN, JINTANG'), whose name is the licensee legal name of a sole trader, not a contact person.

ASIC 'business name' column, free of tilde separators, present on 34.5% of rows and clearly a trading/display name (e.g. 'DISCOVERY FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT' for LUNAWAVE PTY. LIMITED), not the registered name.
11-digit shape on 420/464 rows and 90.5% pass the ABN checksum; the mixed label ABN_ACN means a few rows hold 9-digit ACNs or 0, which the abn transform rejects (null). No ACN is derived.
Suburb/locality column, 100% present, matches AU place names.
Two-letter AU state abbreviations, 8 distinct, all within the enum.
Licence start date, all values DD/MM/YYYY (day-first; values like 21/12/2010 and 28/02/2011 confirm day-first).
Licence end date in DD/MM/YYYY; empty on all discovery rows (current licences) so valid_to is null = still current.

constants.rationale: ASIC Australian credit licence register; all localities/states are Australian.

The dataset is the CURRENT register and CRED_LIC_STATUS is 'APPR' (approved) on 100% of discovery rows with no end dates, so records describe active licensees; status here reflects licence status, not strictly company status.
No explicit entity-type column; names suggest companies but many licensees are individuals/trusts, so left as unknown.

unmapped.reason: Constant 'Credit Licence' on every row; identifies the register, no entity attribute.
Credit licence number - identifier of the licence (record), not a business identifier; used as record_id.
Licence status code (APPR) - single value on all discovery rows and reflects licence state rather than an allowed entity.status enum semantically; constant 'active' used instead on entity.status.
AFS licence number; frequently '0' (425/464) and duplicates the credit licence number when present; not an entity identifier in the ontology and not an ABN/ACN.
Free-text narrative of licence conditions/status changes for the licence; no ontology target and too sparse (0.2%) to be reliable.
Latitude of the licensee address; no coordinate target in the ontology.
Longitude of the licensee address; no coordinate target in the ontology.
External dispute resolution scheme membership (AFCA/FOS/COSL); no ontology target.
Long free-text description of the credit activities authorised by the licence; narrative, no ontology target.

config.notes: TSV, UTF-8 with BOM, 17 columns, tab-delimited per evidence (16 tabs per line). CRED_LIC_ABN_ACN mixes ABNs (11 digit, 90.5% checksum-valid) with ACNs/0; only the ABN path is taken and invalid values resolve to null rather than erroring. No observed_at column exists in the data so resource_last_modified fallback is used. entity.status constant 'active' is inferred from 'Current register' + APPR status; confidence kept moderate.

fields.reason: ASIC register licensee name is the registered-style entity name; individuals like 'LATASH, EDDIE' are sole-trader licensee names, not contacts. Reasonable.
Business name column is a display/trading name distinct from registered name (e.g. DISCOVERY FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT under LUNAWAVE PTY. LIMITED). Correct semantics.

Mixed ABN/ACN column: 11-digit values are ABNs, but 9-digit values (e.g. HEAJAS PTY LTD '601283201') are ACNs dropped by the abn transform. The records shown all pass the checksum, but the source mixes two identifiers and discarding ACNs loses data; an 11-digit value could also in principle be a padded ACN. Mapping an ABN validator onto an ABN/ACN column is defensible only as far as the checksum type is confirmed per row.
Suburb/locality values match AU place names.
Two-letter AU state abbreviations map to the enum.
4-digit AU postcode values match.
DD/MM/YYYY day-first parse is correct for these values (e.g. 20/02/2019, 14/02/2011 with day > 12 confirming).
Empty end dates on current licences map to null valid_to as documented.
Constant AU is consistent with all localities/states shown.

Constant 'active' from CRED_LIC_STATUS='APPR' conflates licence approval status with entity company status; the source code was explicitly left unmapped. Semantics differ between licence status and company status, but no better evidence exists; storing a constant 'active' overstates knowledge and should arguably be 'unknown'.
No explicit type column; defaulting to unknown is correct per ontology guidance.

missed.reason: 9-digit values in this mixed column (e.g. 601283201) are ACNs; the mapping drops them entirely rather than emitting entity.acn.

The only explicit status evidence for the licence holder was left unmapped and replaced by a guessed constant 'active'; it should at least be recorded and, if not semantically a company status, entity.status should be 'unknown'.

critic.summary: Core identity (legal_name, trading_name) and geographic fields (locality/state/postcode/country) are mapped semantically correctly, and the day-first date parse is validated by the sample. Two weak points: (1) CRED_LIC_ABN_ACN is a mixed ABN/ACN column, and only 11-digit values are kept while 9-digit ACNs are discarded — entity.acn should be populated from those; the ABN validator is a reasonable safeguard but does not resolve the mixed-axis issue. (2) entity.status is hard-coded from an assumed licence-approval constant while the explicit status column was left unmapped, effectively a guess overriding source evidence; entity.status should remain 'unknown' unless the source code is genuinely a status enum. entity_type='unknown' is correct. No trading-name-as-legal-name, contact-name, or licence-number-as-identifier errors were found.

config.notes: Revision: CRED_LIC_ABN_ACN is a mixed ABN/ACN column. Shape filters (^\d{11}$ -> entity.abn, ^\d{9}$ -> entity.acn) send only the matching identifier type to its own checksum transform; 7-8 digit and '0' values are treated as missing. This removed all ABN_LENGTH errors (previously 8.8%) and recovers the ACNs that were being discarded. No ACN is ever derived from an ABN. entity.status changed to 'unknown' because CRED_LIC_STATUS is a licence-approval code, not a company status; the column is recorded in unmapped. No observed_at column exists, so resource_last_modified is used. TSV confirmed by 16 tabs per line in raw bytes.

fields.reason: CRED_LIC_NAME is the ASIC register name of the licensee; for individuals it is the person's legal name, not a contact person. The mapping correctly does not treat names as trading names.
CRED_LIC_BN is the business/trading name column; only present where a distinct trading name exists, and the observations show proper trading names, not legal names.

The combined ABN_ACN column is filtered to 11-digit values and passed through an ABN checksum. The held-out values (e.g. 51624785486, 19004493789) are valid ABN-shaped, and no ACN is being mis-typed as ABN.
The same combined column, filtered to 9-digit values and checksummed as ACN. The observed value 601283201 is a valid ACN, taken explicitly from the source, not derived from an ABN.
Direct locality column, values are Australian suburbs/localities. No postal-vs-premises confusion apparent.
Two-letter AU state abbreviations mapped to the enum; all held-out values (NSW, QLD, VIC, WA) are valid enum members.
4-digit AU postcode column; values match the locality/state.
DD/MM/YYYY parsed explicitly day-first; held-out values like 20/02/2019, 06/05/2020 are consistent with day-first and the stated format.
Empty end dates are mapped to null, which the ontology defines as still current. The parse format is day-first, consistent with valid_from.
ASIC Australian credit licence register; all held-out localities/states are Australian.
No entity-status column exists; CRED_LIC_STATUS is a licence approval code ('APPR'), correctly not conflated with entity status. Defaulting to unknown is the safe choice.
No explicit entity-type column; names suggest companies for most rows but include individuals (e.g. 'LATASH, EDDIE'), so unknown is correct per ontology guidance.

missed.reason: The free-text authorisations describe the credit activities (e.g. 'engage in credit activities'), which could support an ANZSIC or activity classification, though it is narrative rather than a code. Not a strong direct match, but it is the only source of activity/industry information.
External dispute resolution scheme membership is not an industry code; this is a weak/no match and is reasonably left unmapped.

critic.summary: The mapping is sound for all held-out fields: legal vs trading names are correctly distinguished, ABN/ACN are correctly separated by shape and validated by checksum, address fields are correctly sourced, dates are parsed day-first, and entity.status/entity_type are left as unknown rather than guessed. No clear ontology target was left unmapped; CRED_LIC_EDRS and CRED_LIC_AUTHORISATIONS have no strong ontology match.
